title: Fire Prevention Week, 2025
summary:
The proclamation designates October 5–11, 2025 as Fire Prevention Week, urging families and communities to reduce fire risks and honoring firefighters and first responders. It also highlights new federal steps aimed at improving wildfire prevention, faster response, and household safety.

The document points to recent deadly wildfires in California as evidence of the costs of poor preparation. It places blame on state and local leadership and on certain policy approaches, and then describes actions the Administration says will reverse course. These include consolidating wildland fire programs within federal departments, encouraging local preparedness and response, using new tools like artificial intelligence and better data sharing to spot and fight fires sooner, and reviewing how the Federal Emergency Management Agency handles disasters. It also notes an order to speed up recovery efforts in California and references what it calls the largest wildfire hazardous waste cleanup in the Environmental Protection Agency’s history. The proclamation thanks firefighters, first responders, infrastructure workers, and volunteers, and points to newly enacted permanent pay increases for federal wildland firefighters. Families are encouraged to make escape plans, test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms monthly, and reduce common home hazards like unattended cooking and faulty wiring.

Who stands to benefit most are firefighters and first responders through pay and recognition, communities through added coordination and technology, and households through clear safety steps. People and agencies affected by program consolidation or shifts in responsibility may face changes or uncertainty, and some state and local leaders may take issue with the blame placed on them. Others may be concerned about the tone of the proclamation or debate the causes of recent fires, the balance of federal and local roles, and whether these measures go far enough.
